il_e_goreville_theatre.blurb: A sandstone sport wall inside Ferne Clyffe State Park near Goreville, in far southern Illinois. All 17 routes are bolted, and the grades lean hard: one 5.8, one 5.9, a few 5.10s, then a solid block of 5.11 and 5.12 climbs. Several lines leave from a raised ledge that looks like a stage, which gives the wall its name. The lower-angle climbs are delicate, technical slabs, while the steeper ground is face climbing at the upper end of the range. It is the fifth zone you reach when walking along the base of the cliffs from the lot, so it makes a natural stop on a day spent working through the park's walls.

il_h_wizard_wall.blurb: A long sandstone cliff at Jackson Falls in southern Illinois, strung between The Gallery and the North Falls section and only a couple of minutes from North Falls on foot. It holds 16 routes, 11 of them sport and 5 trad, running from a few 5.9s up to 5.13. The bulk sit in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, so it suits climbers already comfortable on steeper, sustained sandstone, though the 5.9 trad and sport lines give a way in at the lower end. Stand & Deliver is the most ticked line here, and the hardest route on the wall is a 5.13a.

il_a_the_gallery.blurb: One of the busiest sandstone walls at Jackson Falls in southern Illinois, sitting in the West Falls section. It has 16 routes, mostly bolted sport lines with a pair of trad climbs and one easy 5.6 top-rope chimney. Most of the grades cluster at 5.10, with a handful of 5.9s and a spread of 5.11 and 5.12 climbs above them, so it is friendly to climbers stepping up from moderates. The wall catches sun nearly all day and is among the first to dry after rain, and the lines tend to be consistently good, with big holds and a pumpy character. Expect company on a fair weekend.

il_e_spleef_peak.blurb: A big free-standing block of sandstone beside the main waterfall at Jackson Falls in southern Illinois, listed with the North Falls climbing. It carries 16 climbs: mostly bolted sport routes, plus one top-rope line and a single boulder problem. Grades run from 5.8 up to 5.13, with the weight in the 5.10 to 5.13 range, so there is a little warm-up terrain and a lot for people projecting. The block stands apart from the cliff line, which makes it easy to find, and several of the routes on it are well regarded classics for the canyon.
